CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

STATUSLINE SETUP NEEDED: The caveman plugin includes a statusline badge showing active mode (e.g. [CAVEMAN], [CAVEMAN:ULTRA]). It is not configured yet. To enable, add this to /Users/praveensam/.claude-work/settings.json: "statusLine": { "type": "command", "command": "bash \"/Users/praveensam/.claude-work/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/ef6050c5e184/hooks/caveman-statusline.sh\"" } Proactively offer to set this up for the user on first interaction.

message.content: I want to configure a few integrations and test a simple full user-friendly workflow. Guide me

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) on a cron schedule or once at a specific time. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring or one-time remote agent ("run this every Monday", "open a cleanup PR for X in 2 weeks"), or to manage existing routines. ALSO OFFER PROACTIVELY: after you finish work that has a natural future follow-up, end your reply with a one-line offer to schedule a background agent to do it. Strong signals: a feature flag / gate / experiment / staged rollout was just shipped (offer a one-time agent in ~2 weeks to open a cleanup PR or evaluate results), a new alert/monitor was created (offer a recurring agent to triage it), a TODO/migration with a "remove once X" condition was left behind (offer a one-time agent to do the removal). Skip the offer for refactors, bug fixes, and anything that is done once it ships. Name a concrete action and cadence ("in 2 weeks", "every Monday") and only offer when the run just succeeded — do not pitch a schedule for something that has not happened yet.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.

# Product Requirements Document - autom9                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                    
  **Date:** 2026-04-08                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                    
  ## Executive Summary                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                    
  autom9 is a Tableau dashboard extension that embeds an AI agent directly into the planning tool consultants already use as their system of record.
  The agent enables consultants to complete planning workflows — submitting Smartsheet requests, creating Google Calendar invites, picking up open  
  work — without leaving Tableau. The core insight: the problem is not data visibility, which Tableau already solves, but the broken link between   
  seeing data and acting on it. Every alternative requires pulling data out of context; autom9 closes that loop inside the tool.                    
                                                                                                                                                    
  The POC targets ~80 consultants at a professional services firm. The underlying platform — BYOM (OpenAI and Anthropic), JSON-configured workflows,
  no external automation dependency — is designed to support multiple agent use cases beyond the initial planning assistant. The POC proves the     
  value of the first use case and the extensibility of the platform simultaneously.                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                    
  ### What Makes This Special                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                    
  **Workflow completion in a single surface.** Tableau is where consultants review their planning data; autom9 is where they act on it — same tab,  
  same context, no handoff to Slack, Smartsheet, or email. This is architecturally only possible as a native Tableau Extension.                     
                                                                                                                                                    
  **BYOM + JSON-driven extensibility.** New agent workflows are added via configuration, not bespoke engineering. The platform is explicitly        
  designed                                                                                                                                          
  to support a growing library of agent workflows. This directly counters Salesforce Einstein's model-locked, CRM-centric approach to AI in Tableau.
                                                                                                                                                    
  **No direct competitor.** No commercially available Tableau extension offers BYOM agentic workflows with external tool integration. The           
  competitive window is estimated at 12–18 months before Salesforce closes it with a native Agentforce integration.                                 
                                                                                                                                                    
  --------                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                    
  **Project Type** | B2B SaaS / Platform                                                                                                            
  **Domain** | AI / Workflow Automation                                                                                                             
  **Complexity** | Medium                                                                                                                           
  **Project Context** | Greenfield                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                    
  ## Success Criteria                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                    
  ### User Success                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                    
  • **Primary metric:** 60%+ of the 80 POC consultants complete at least one Smartsheet planning request via the extension per week within 60 days  
  of launch. Google Calendar invite creation is tracked but optional for this threshold.                                                            
  • **Qualitative signal:** Testimonials from consultants citing measurable reduction in time spent on scheduling logistics and fewer context       
  switches across tools.                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                    
  ### Business Success                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                    
  • POC demonstrates genuine, repeatable value for the target user group — evidenced by adoption rate and qualitative feedback.                     
  • Platform extensibility validated internally by configuring and deploying at least one additional agent workflow via the JSON system (post-POC,  
  not a v1 deliverable).                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                    
  ### Technical Success                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                    
  • All agent interactions logged with sufficient detail to diagnose issues, trace failed tool calls, and identify latency patterns.                
  • Agent responses complete within 20 seconds during the POC phase (nice-to-have; no hard SLA in v1).                                              
  • Extension architecture supports future air-gapped deployment — local LLM integration and fully local install. Design constraint for v1, not a v1
  deliverable.                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                    
  ### Measurable Outcomes                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                    
   Metric                                         | Target                                        | Timeframe                                       
  ------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------  
   Weekly active users (workflow completion)      | 60%+ of 80 consultants                        | 60 days post-launch                             
   Smartsheet requests submitted via extension    | Tracked per user                              | Ongoing                                         
   Agent response time (p95)                      | ≤20 seconds (nice-to-have)                    | POC phase                                       
   Failed/errored agent interactions              | Logged and reviewable                         | At launch                                       
                                                                                                                                                    
  ## Product Scope                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                    
  ### MVP — Minimum Viable Product                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                    
  • Consultant planning view: open days surfaced from Snowflake via Tableau data source                                                             
  • Task ingestion from individual Google Docs with clarifying Q&A in the chat panel                                                                
  • Smartsheet planning request trigger from the extension                                                                                          
  • Google Calendar invite creation around existing engagements                                                                                     
  • Org-wide open work board (Google Doc) with billable/internal priority logic, availability check, accept/decline flow, and coordinator           
  notification                                                                                                                                      
  • BYOM: OpenAI and Anthropic support                                                                                                              
  • JSON workflow configuration system (versionable)                                                                                                
  • Agent interaction logging (admin diagnostics)                                                                                                   
  • Integration status check on extension load                                                                                                      
  • Token-based data masking before LLM calls + rehydration after response                                                                          
  • Extension install: Tableau Desktop (development) + Tableau Cloud/Server (production)                                                            
                                                                                                                                                    
  ### Growth Features (Post-MVP)                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                    
  • Per-user data scoping (agent limited to authenticated consultant's own records)                                                                 
  • Group-level credential management                                                                                                               
  • Licensing mechanism: license key in .trex file validated against registered Tableau URL                                                         
  • Slack integration: surface open work requests from emoji-tagged messages                                                                        
  • At least one additional agent workflow configured via JSON (platform extensibility validation)                                                  
  • Expanded logging and analytics: adoption dashboards, workflow completion rates                                                                  
  • Additional BYOM model support                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                    
  ### Vision (Future)                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                    
  • Self-hosted premium tier: customer-managed infrastructure, no external data dependency                                                          
  • Local LLM support for air-gapped environments                                                                                                   
  • Open marketplace of Tableau agent workflows                                                                                                     
  • Manager/team-level views across multiple consultants                                                                                            
  • Consulting Accelerator: packaged product for professional services firms

import sys

from cryptography.fernet import Fernet
from pydantic import ValidationError, field_validator
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_file=".env", extra="ignore")

    DATABASE_URL: str
    ENCRYPTION_KEY: str
    BACKEND_SECRET: str

    @field_validator("ENCRYPTION_KEY")
    @classmethod
    def encryption_key_valid(cls, v: str) -> str:
        try:
            Fernet(v.encode())
        except Exception as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"ENCRYPTION_KEY is not a valid Fernet key: {exc}") from exc
        return v
    LOG_LEVEL: str
    DATABASE_POOL_BASE: int
    DATABASE_POOL_OVERFLOW: int
    CORS_ORIGINS: str = "http://localhost:5173"
    SMARTSHEET_API_TOKEN: str | None = None
    SMARTSHEET_SHEET_ID: str | None = None
    GOOGLE_CALENDAR_CLIENT_ID: str | None = None
    GOOGLE_CALENDAR_CLIENT_SECRET: str | None = None
    GOOGLE_CALENDAR_REFRESH_TOKEN: str | None = None
    GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID: str = "primary"
    GOOGLE_DOCS_CLIENT_ID: str | None = None
    GOOGLE_DOCS_CLIENT_SECRET: str | None = None
    GOOGLE_DOCS_REFRESH_TOKEN: str | None = None


try:
    settings = Settings()
except ValidationError as e:
    print(f"Configuration error — missing or invalid environment variables:\n{e}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)

import uuid

from typing import Literal

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException
from sqlalchemy import select, update
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.api.deps import require_admin
from app.db.deps import get_db
from app.models.credential_store import CredentialStore
from app.schemas.credentials import CredentialGetResponse, CredentialUpsertRequest, CredentialUpsertResponse
from app.schemas.status import Meta
from app.services.encryption import encrypt

_Provider = Literal["openai", "anthropic"]

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/admin/credentials", tags=["admin"])

_ORG_ID = "default"
_MASKED = "••••••••"


@router.post("", status_code=200, response_model=CredentialUpsertResponse, dependencies=[Depends(require_admin)])
async def upsert_credential(
    body: CredentialUpsertRequest,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
) -> CredentialUpsertResponse:
    encrypted = encrypt(body.api_key)

    # Deactivate all providers for this org — one active at a time
    await db.execute(
        update(CredentialStore)
        .where(CredentialStore.org_id == _ORG_ID)
        .values(is_active=False)
    )

    result = await db.execute(
        select(CredentialStore).where(
            CredentialStore.org_id == _ORG_ID,
            CredentialStore.provider == body.provider,
        )
    )
    row = result.scalar_one_or_none()
    if row is None:
        new_row = CredentialStore(
            org_id=_ORG_ID,
            provider=body.provider,
            encrypted_key=encrypted,
            is_active=True,
        )
        db.add(new_row)
        try:
            await db.flush()
        except IntegrityError:
            # Concurrent upsert won the race — rollback savepoint and update instead
            await db.rollback()
            # Rollback also undid the bulk deactivation — re-apply it
            await db.execute(
                update(CredentialStore)
                .where(CredentialStore.org_id == _ORG_ID)
                .values(is_active=False)
            )
            result2 = await db.execute(
                select(CredentialStore).where(
                    CredentialStore.org_id == _ORG_ID,
                    CredentialStore.provider == body.provider,
                )
            )
            existing = result2.scalar_one()
            existing.encrypted_key = encrypted
            existing.is_active = True
    else:
        row.encrypted_key = encrypted
        row.is_active = True

    return CredentialUpsertResponse(
        data={"provider": body.provider, "masked_key": _MASKED},
        meta=Meta(request_id=str(uuid.uuid4())),
    )


@router.get("/{provider}", status_code=200, response_model=CredentialGetResponse, dependencies=[Depends(require_admin)])
async def get_credential(
    provider: _Provider,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
) -> CredentialGetResponse:
    result = await db.execute(
        select(CredentialStore).where(
            CredentialStore.org_id == _ORG_ID,
            CredentialStore.provider == provider,
        )
    )
    row = result.scalar_one_or_none()
    if row is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"No credentials for provider '{provider}'")
    return CredentialGetResponse(
        data={"provider": row.provider, "masked_key": _MASKED},
        meta=Meta(request_id=str(uuid.uuid4())),
    )

import asyncio
import logging
import time
import uuid

from fastapi import APIRouter, Header
from typing import Annotated

from app.integrations import ALL_INTEGRATIONS, IntegrationStatus
from app.schemas.status import IntegrationStatusItem, StatusData, StatusResponse, Meta

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter(prefix="/api", tags=["status"])


_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S = 5.0


async def _run_health_check(integration) -> IntegrationStatusItem:
    """Wraps one integration health_check with timing and per-check timeout."""
    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        result: IntegrationStatus = await asyncio.wait_for(
            integration.health_check(), timeout=_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S
        )
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        return IntegrationStatusItem(
            name=integration.name,
            status="unavailable",
            latency_ms=int(_HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S * 1000),
            error="health check timed out",
        )
    latency_ms = int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000)
    return IntegrationStatusItem(
        name=result.name,
        status=result.status,
        latency_ms=latency_ms,
        error=result.error,
    )


@router.get("/status", response_model=StatusResponse)
async def get_status(
    x_autom9_session: Annotated[str | None, Header()] = None,
) -> StatusResponse:
    """
    Runs parallel health checks against all configured integrations.
    Returns results regardless of individual integration status — failure isolation (NFR9).
    Each check times out at 5 seconds (NFR2, NFR8). Contract violations caught via return_exceptions.
    """
    session_id = x_autom9_session or "unknown"
    request_id = str(uuid.uuid4())

    raw = await asyncio.gather(
        *[_run_health_check(integration) for integration in ALL_INTEGRATIONS],
        return_exceptions=True,
    )

    results: list[IntegrationStatusItem] = []
    for idx, item in enumerate(raw):
        if isinstance(item, BaseException):
            results.append(IntegrationStatusItem(
                name=ALL_INTEGRATIONS[idx].name,
                status="unavailable",
                latency_ms=None,
                error=f"unexpected error: {type(item).__name__}",
            ))
        else:
            results.append(item)

    for result in results:
        logger.info(
            "integration_health_check",
            extra={
                "session_id": session_id,
                "integration": result.name,
                "status": result.status,
                "latency_ms": result.latency_ms,
                # NOTE: no credentials, no user PII logged here
            },
        )

    return StatusResponse(
        data=StatusData(integrations=results),
        meta=Meta(request_id=request_id),
    )

import asyncio
import logging
import time
import uuid
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Header, HTTPException
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.agent.provider_factory import get_provider
from app.api.deps import require_admin
from app.core.exceptions import IntegrationError, ProviderError
from app.db.deps import get_db
from app.integrations import ALL_INTEGRATIONS
from app.schemas.status import IntegrationStatusItem, IntegrationTestResponse, Meta

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/integrations", tags=["integrations"])

_INTEGRATION_MAP = {i.name: i for i in ALL_INTEGRATIONS}
# Valid names: "smartsheet", "google_calendar", "google_docs", "tableau_data", "llm"
_VALID_NAMES = set(_INTEGRATION_MAP.keys()) | {"llm"}

# Admin test has more time than load health check (5s) — admin is deliberately waiting
_TEST_TIMEOUT_S = 10.0


@router.post(
    "/{name}/test",
    response_model=IntegrationTestResponse,
    dependencies=[Depends(require_admin)],
)
async def test_integration(
    name: str,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
    x_autom9_session: Annotated[str | None, Header()] = None,
) -> IntegrationTestResponse:
    """
    Admin-only on-demand connectivity test for a named integration.
    Returns a single IntegrationStatusItem — never raises on integration failure (NFR9).
    Valid names: smartsheet, google_calendar, google_docs, tableau_data, llm.
    """
    if name not in _VALID_NAMES:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Unknown integration '{name}'")

    session_id = x_autom9_session or "unknown"

    if name == "llm":
        result = await _test_llm(db)
    else:
        result = await _test_integration(name)

    logger.info(
        "integration_connection_test",
        extra={
            "session_id": session_id,
            "integration": result.name,
            "status": result.status,
            "latency_ms": result.latency_ms,
            # NOTE: no credentials, no user PII logged here (FR19)
        },
    )

    return IntegrationTestResponse(
        data=result,
        meta=Meta(request_id=str(uuid.uuid4())),
    )


async def _test_integration(name: str) -> IntegrationStatusItem:
    """Calls health_check() for a named IntegrationBase implementation."""
    integration = _INTEGRATION_MAP[name]
    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        status = await asyncio.wait_for(
            integration.health_check(), timeout=_TEST_TIMEOUT_S
        )
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        return IntegrationStatusItem(
            name=name,
            status="unavailable",
            latency_ms=int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000),
            error="connection test timed out",
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        return IntegrationStatusItem(
            name=name,
            status="unavailable",
            latency_ms=int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000),
            error=str(exc) or "health check failed",
        )
    latency_ms = int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000)
    return IntegrationStatusItem(
        name=status.name,
        status=status.status,
        latency_ms=latency_ms,
        error=status.error,
    )


async def _test_llm(db: AsyncSession) -> IntegrationStatusItem:
    """
    Tests LLM provider connectivity.
    Resolves active provider from DB via get_provider(), then makes a minimal completion call.
    Returns unavailable if no credentials configured or if the API call fails.
    """
    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        provider = await get_provider(db)
        await asyncio.wait_for(
            provider.complete([{"role": "user", "content": "ping"}], []),
            timeout=_TEST_TIMEOUT_S,
        )
        latency_ms = int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000)
        return IntegrationStatusItem(
            name="llm",
            status="healthy",
            latency_ms=latency_ms,
            error=None,
        )
    except ProviderError as exc:
        latency_ms = int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000)
        return IntegrationStatusItem(
            name="llm",
            status="unavailable",
            latency_ms=latency_ms,
            error=str(exc),
        )
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        return IntegrationStatusItem(
            name="llm",
            status="unavailable",
            latency_ms=int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000),
            error="LLM connection test timed out",
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        return IntegrationStatusItem(
            name="llm",
            status="unavailable",
            latency_ms=int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000),
            error=str(exc) or "LLM connection test failed",
        )

from app.integrations import ALL_INTEGRATIONS

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/integrations", tags=["integrations"])

_INTEGRATION_MAP = {i.name: i for i in ALL_INTEGRATIONS}
# Valid names: "smartsheet", "google_calendar", "google_docs", "tableau_data", "llm"
_VALID_NAMES = set(_INTEGRATION_MAP.keys()) | {"llm"}

# Admin test has more time than load health check (5s) — admin is deliberately waiting
_TEST_TIMEOUT_S = 10.0


@router.post(
    "/{name}/test",
    response_model=IntegrationTestResponse,
    dependencies=[Depends(require_admin)],
)
async def test_integration(
    name: str,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
    x_autom9_session: Annotated[str | None, Header()] = None,
) -> IntegrationTestResponse:
    """
    Admin-only on-demand connectivity test for a named integration.
    Returns a single IntegrationStatusItem — never raises on integration failure (NFR9).
    Valid names: smartsheet, google_calendar, google_docs, tableau_data, llm.
    """
    if name not in _VALID_NAMES:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Unknown integration '{name}'")

    session_id = x_autom9_session or "unknown"

    if name == "llm":
        result = await _test_llm(db)
    else:
        result = await _test_integration(name)

    logger.info(
        "integration_connection_test",
        extra={
            "session_id": session_id,
            "integration": result.name,
            "status": result.status,
            "latency_ms": result.latency_ms,
            # NOTE: no credentials, no user PII logged here (FR19)
        },
    )

    return IntegrationTestResponse(
        data=result,
        meta=Meta(request_id=str(uuid.uuid4())),
    )


async def _test_integration(name: str) -> IntegrationStatusItem:
    """Calls health_check() for a named IntegrationBase implementation."""
    integration = _INTEGRATION_MAP[name]
    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        status = await asyncio.wait_for(
            integration.health_check(), timeout=_TEST_TIMEOUT_S
        )
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        return IntegrationStatusItem(
            name=name,
            status="unavailable",
            latency_ms=int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000),
            error="connection test timed out",
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        return IntegrationStatusItem(
            name=name,
            status="unavailable",
            latency_ms=int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000),
            error=str(exc) or "health check failed",
        )
    latency_ms = int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000)
    return IntegrationStatusItem(
        name=status.name,
        status=status.status,
        latency_ms=latency_ms,
        error=status.error,
    )


async def _test_llm(db: AsyncSession) -> IntegrationStatusItem:
    """
    Tests LLM provider connectivity.
    Resolves active provider from DB via get_provider(), then makes a minimal completion call.
    Returns unavailable if no credentials configured or if the API call fails.
    """
    start = time.monotonic()
    try:
        provider = await get_provider(db)
        await asyncio.wait_for(
            provider.complete([{"role": "user", "content": "ping"}], []),
            timeout=_TEST_TIMEOUT_S,
        )
        latency_ms = int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000)
        return IntegrationStatusItem(
            name="llm",
            status="healthy",
            latency_ms=latency_ms,
            error=None,
        )
    except ProviderError as exc:
        latency_ms = int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000)
        return IntegrationStatusItem(
            name="llm",
            status="unavailable",
            latency_ms=latency_ms,
            error=str(exc),
        )
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        return IntegrationStatusItem(
            name="llm",
            status="unavailable",
            latency_ms=int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000),
            error="LLM connection test timed out",
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        return IntegrationStatusItem(
            name="llm",
            status="unavailable",
            latency_ms=int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000),
            error=str(exc) or "LLM connection test failed",
        )

import json
import uuid
from json import JSONDecodeError

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, Request
from pydantic import ValidationError
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.api.deps import require_admin
from app.config.workflow_registry import workflow_registry
from app.db.deps import get_db
from app.schemas.config import WorkflowConfigUploadResponse
from app.schemas.status import Meta

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/admin/config", tags=["admin"])


@router.post("", status_code=200, response_model=WorkflowConfigUploadResponse,
             dependencies=[Depends(require_admin)])
async def upload_workflow_config(
    request: Request,
    db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db),
) -> WorkflowConfigUploadResponse:
    """Upload and activate a new JSON workflow config.

    Request body must be the raw JSON config object (Content-Type: application/json).
    Returns 422 with structured error if schema validation fails.
    Previous active config is preserved on any error.
    """
    try:
        body: dict = await request.json()
    except JSONDecodeError:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Request body is not valid JSON")

    try:
        row = await workflow_registry.register_workflow(body, db)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        first = exc.errors(include_url=False)[0]
        field = str(first["loc"][-1]) if first.get("loc") else "input"
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail=f"{field}: {first['msg']}")

    return WorkflowConfigUploadResponse(
        data={
            "version": row.version,
            "workflow_id": body.get("workflow_id", ""),
            "tool_count": len(body.get("tools", [])),
        },
        meta=Meta(request_id=str(uuid.uuid4())),
    )

# Developer Walk-Me Guide                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                    
  ### How to navigate, test, and extend autom9                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                    
  This guide assumes you have Docker, Node.js, and uv installed but limited familiarity with the codebase. It covers first boot, making and         
  verifying a code change, and how all the pieces connect.                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                    
  --------                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                    
  ## 1. What the project is                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                    
  autom9 is two things:                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                    
   Part                                           | What it is                                    | Where it lives                                  
  ------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------  
   **Backend**                                    | Python/FastAPI REST API                       | autom9-backend/                                 
   **Extension**                                  | Tableau extension (Svelte/TypeScript UI)      | autom9-extension/                               
                                                                                                                                                    
  The backend connects to Postgres, talks to LLMs (OpenAI/Anthropic), and integrates with external tools (Google Calendar, Google Docs, Smartsheet).
  The extension is embedded inside Tableau and calls the backend API.                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                    
  --------                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                    
  ## 2. First-time setup                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                    
  ### 2a. Environment file                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                    
    cp autom9-backend/.env.example autom9-backend/.env                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                    
  The only two values you need to fill in for local dev:                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                    
    ENCRYPTION_KEY=<any 32-byte base64 string>                                                                                                      
    BACKEND_SECRET=<any string, e.g. "localdev">                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                    
  Generate a valid encryption key:                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                    
    cd autom9-backend                                                                                                                               
    uv run python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"                                                
                                                                                                                                                    
  ### 2b. Start the database                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                    
    docker-compose up db                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                    
  Starts Postgres 16 on port 5432. Leave it running.                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                    
  ### 2c. Run migrations                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                    
    cd autom9-backend                                                                                                                               
    uv run alembic upgrade head                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                    
  Only needed once, then again after anyone adds migration files.                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                    
  --------                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                    
  ## 3. Running the backend                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                    
    cd autom9-backend                                                                                                                               
    uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                    
  --reload restarts automatically on every Python file save.                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                    
  Health check:                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                    
    curl http://localhost:8000/health                                                                                                               
    # → {"status":"ok"}                                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                    
  Interactive API explorer (browse and call all endpoints):                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                    
    http://localhost:8000/docs                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                    
  --------                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                    
  ## 4. Running the frontend (extension)                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                    
    cp autom9-extension/.env.example autom9-extension/.env                                                                                          
    # VITE_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8000 (already correct for local dev)                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                    
    cd autom9-extension                                                                                                                             
    npm install                                                                                                                                     
    npm run dev                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                    
  Dev server starts at http://localhost:5173. This runs outside Tableau — some Tableau-specific features will be stubbed, but the panels and API    
  calls work.                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                    
  After any TypeScript/Svelte change, verify the build compiles cleanly:                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                    
    cd autom9-extension && npm run build                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                    
  --------                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                    
  ## 5. Running the tests                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                    
  Tests live in autom9-backend/tests/. They **do not need the server running** — they spin up their own in-memory app. They **do need Postgres      
  running** (docker-compose up db).                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                    
    # Run everything (272 tests as of Story 4.2)                                                                                                    
    cd autom9-backend                                                                                                                               
    uv run pytest -v                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                    
    # Run one file                                                                                                                                  
    uv run pytest tests/integrations/test_google_calendar.py -v                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                    
    # Run one test by name                                                                                                                          
    uv run pytest tests/agent/test_capacity.py::test_check_capacity_sufficient -v                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                    
    # Coverage — see which lines are untested                                                                                                       
    uv run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                    
  **Always use **uv run — never bare python, python3, or pytest.                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                    
  --------                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                    
  ## 6. How the tests work                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                    
  No real LLM keys or Google credentials are needed. Every external call is **mocked** — the tests use fake stand-ins that simulate the real        
  services.                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                    
  tests/conftest.py does this automatically for every test:                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                    
  • Generates a throwaway ENCRYPTION_KEY                                                                                                            
  • Points to autom9_test (a separate local database)                                                                                               
  • Creates all tables before the suite starts, drops them after                                                                                    
  • Wraps each test in a transaction that **rolls back** — dirty data never persists between tests                                                  
                                                                                                                                                    
  When you write a test against the HTTP client, it runs through the real FastAPI app with a fake database session injected. No HTTP calls go to    
  Google, Smartsheet, etc. unless you write one that explicitly does.                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                    
  **Pure-function tests** (e.g., tests/agent/test_capacity.py) need no fixtures at all — they import and call the function directly.

    │   │   ├── capacity.py       ← Pure capacity check function (no I/O, no integrations)                                                          
    │   │   ├── masking.py        ← PII token masking / rehydration (ARC-9: 100% branch coverage)                                                   
    │   │   └── provider_factory.py ← Loads Anthropic or OpenAI provider                                                                            
    │   ├── config/               ← Workflow configuration system

  The backend connects to Postgres, talks to LLMs (OpenAI/Anthropic), and integrates with external tools (Google Calendar, Google Docs, Smartsheet).

**What's running:** DB only (Postgres on 5432). Backend + frontend not started.

**Config flow to test a full workflow:**

```

2. Start backend  → uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
3. Start frontend → cd autom9-extension && npm run dev
4. Open admin     → http://localhost:5173?admin=1
5. Add LLM key    → Anthropic or OpenAI via AdminConfig panel
6. Upload config  → paste docs/example-workflow-config.json
7. Test workflow  → chat: "check my capacity for X days", "submit planning request", "create calendar invite"
```

**Credentials you need to gather:**

| Integration | Env vars needed |

| Smartsheet | `SMARTSHEET_API_TOKEN`, `SMARTSHEET_SHEET_ID` |
| Google Calendar | `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_REFRESH_TOKEN` |
| Google Docs | `GOOGLE_DOCS_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_DOCS_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_DOCS_REFRESH_TOKEN` |

**Which integrations do you want to wire up?**

- All 3 (Smartsheet + both Google)?
- Just one to start (e.g. Smartsheet only)?
- Google Calendar + Docs share an OAuth app — I can walk you through getting the refresh token for both at once.

Tell me what you have / want to start with and I'll guide each step.

With only Google (Calendar + Docs), you can test:

**Google Docs → fetch tasks**
- Paste personal task Google Doc URL in chat
- Agent reads it, lists tasks, answers questions about them

**Google Docs → open work board**
- Point workflow config `open_work_board.google_docs_url` at a doc
- Open Work Panel loads opportunities (billable / internal sections)
- Agent reads them and discusses

**Google Calendar → create invite**
- Ask agent: *"Create a calendar invite for a client meeting May 5th 9–10am"*
- Agent calls `create_invite`, event appears in your Google Calendar

**Capacity check** (no integrations needed)
- Pure logic — works with zero credentials
- Ask: *"I have 8 open days, can I take a 6-day engagement?"*

**LLM integration test** (needs Anthropic or OpenAI key in DB)
- Admin panel → save key → `POST /api/integrations/llm/test`

**What you CAN'T test without Smartsheet:**
- `submit_planning_request` tool — will error with "Smartsheet not configured"

**Recommended minimal test path:**
1. Wire up Google (one OAuth app covers both Calendar + Docs)
2. Add Anthropic key via admin panel
3. Upload workflow config (set `open_work_board.google_docs_url` to a real doc)
4. Chat: capacity check → open work fetch → calendar invite

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |
| **ultra** | Abbreviate prose words (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl), strip conjunctions, arrows for causality (X → Y), one word when one word enough. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never abbreviate |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully 文言文. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (之/乃/為/其) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

- wenyan-ultra: "新參照→重繪。useMemo Wrap。"

- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool = reuse DB conn. Skip handshake → fast under load."

Valid point, but code already uses refresh token flow — `google_calendar.py:55` does `grant_type=refresh_token` on every startup. Client ID + secret alone can't get access tokens without refresh token.

Two paths:

**Option A: OAuth Playground (no script, one-time manual)**
1. Go to `developers.google.com/oauthplayground`
2. Gear icon → check "Use your own OAuth credentials" → paste client_id + secret
3. Left panel → add scopes manually:

   - `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/documents.readonly`
4. Authorize APIs → Exchange for tokens
5. Copy `refresh_token` → paste into `.env`

**Option B: Service account** (more stable, no expiry concern)
- Different credentials type in Google Cloud
- Share calendar + docs with service account email
- Uses JWT, no refresh token needed
- Requires code changes in both integrations

Option A = 5 min, no code change. Option B = more robust long-term but needs refactor.

**2. Open work board** (`open_work_board.google_docs_url`)

Structured with **Google Docs heading styles** (not bold — actual Heading 1/2/3):

```
Billable          ← Heading style, text must be "Billable" or "Client Work"
Project Alpha     ← Normal text → becomes opportunity title
• 5 days required
• Starts June 2026
• SAP experience needed

Project Beta      ← another opportunity
• 3 days

Internal          ← Heading style, text must be "Internal" or "Internal Work"
Tech talk prep    ← opportunity title
• 1 day
• Optional
```

- Section header must be **heading style** (H1–H6) AND text exactly matches `billable`/`client work`/`internal`/`internal work` (case-insensitive)
- Normal paragraph = new opportunity title
- Bullet paragraph = appended to last opportunity's details

import logging
import uuid

from fastapi import APIRouter, Header, HTTPException

from app.config.workflow_registry import workflow_registry
from app.core.exceptions import IntegrationError
from app.integrations.google_docs import GoogleDocsIntegration
from app.schemas.data import OpportunityItem, OpenWorkResponse, TaskItem, TasksResponse
from app.schemas.status import Meta

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/data", tags=["data"])

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_google_docs = GoogleDocsIntegration()


@router.get(
    "/tasks",
    response_model=TasksResponse,
    status_code=200,
)
async def get_tasks(
    x_autom9_session: str | None = Header(default=None),
) -> TasksResponse:
    """
    Fetch consultant task list from the configured Google Doc.

    Reads google_docs_url from the active workflow config's data_panel section.
    Returns 503 if integration is unavailable.
    Returns 404 if no data_panel config is present.
    No admin auth required — accessible to any session holder (same as /api/status).
    """
    active = workflow_registry.active_config
    if active is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="No workflow config loaded")

    data_panel = active.get("data_panel")
    if not data_panel:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="data_panel not configured")

    google_docs_url = data_panel.get("google_docs_url")
    if not google_docs_url:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="google_docs_url not configured")

    logger.info(
        "data_tasks_fetch",
        extra={
            "session_id": x_autom9_session or "unknown",
            "integration": "google_docs",
        },
    )

    try:
        result = await _google_docs.execute("fetch_tasks", {"url": google_docs_url})
    except IntegrationError as exc:
        logger.warning(
            "data_tasks_fetch_failed",
            extra={"integration": exc.integration, "error": str(exc)},
        )
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail=str(exc)) from exc

    tasks = [TaskItem(text=str(item)) for item in result.get("tasks", [])]
    return TasksResponse(data=tasks, meta=Meta(request_id=str(uuid.uuid4())))


@router.get(
    "/open-work",
    response_model=OpenWorkResponse,
    status_code=200,
)
async def get_open_work(
    x_autom9_session: str | None = Header(default=None),
) -> OpenWorkResponse:
    """
    Fetch org-wide open work opportunities from the configured Google Doc.

    Reads google_docs_url from the active workflow config's open_work_board section.
    Returns opportunities sorted: billable first, internal second.
    Returns 503 if integration is unavailable.
    Returns 404 if no open_work_board config is present.
    """
    active = workflow_registry.active_config
    if active is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="No workflow config loaded")

    open_work_board = active.get("open_work_board")
    if not open_work_board:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="open_work_board not configured")

# Actions registered here auto-execute without consultant confirmation (read/compute only).

def _run_check_capacity(params: dict, available_days: float | None) -> dict:

        )

    if raw is None:
        raise IntegrationError("check_capacity", "required_days parameter is required")

@router.post("", response_model=ChatResponse, status_code=200)

    body: ChatRequest,

    Primary agent interaction endpoint.

    Two modes:
    - Normal turn (body.message set): mask input, call LLM, return reply or pending_action.
    - Confirm turn (body.confirm_action set): execute tool via registry, call LLM for final reply.

    Masking pipeline (FR17, FR18): session_context fields registered before mask_text.
    Logs masked_input/masked_output only (NFR7).

        )

            history=body.history,

            db=db,

        message=body.message or "",
        history=body.history,

        db=db,
        active_config=active,
